title: Local finite type descends through an fppf source cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A morphism is representable by algebraic spaces if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. For representable maps, flatness, local finite presentation and local finite type are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts, up to isomorphism, after some field extension [def-weil-field]. Let $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $g:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$, both representable by algebraic spaces. Suppose $h$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. If $g h$ is locally of finite type, then $g$ is locally of finite type. No quasi-compactness of $h$ and no Noetherian assumption on any stack is required.

source.place: Tag 06EW (lemma-locally-finite-type-fppf-local-source), extended to representable stack morphisms by their scheme-base-change tests. This is local finite type, not Tag 06EV on local finite presentation.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T\to\mathcal C$. Put $B_T=T\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$ and $A_T=B_T\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$. The first is an algebraic space by representability of $g$; the second is an algebraic space by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space] applied to $h$. The map $h_T:A_T\to B_T$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by base-change stability [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. There is a canonical identification $A_T\simeq T\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A$: an object $(t,b,\alpha:g(b)\simeq t,a,\beta:h(a)\simeq b)$ is sent to $(t,a,\alpha\circ g(\beta))$, and its inverse takes $b=h(a)$ and $\beta=1$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Consequently $p:A_T\to T$ is the base change of $gh$ and is locally of finite type by the same calculus node.

Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $v:V\to B_T$ and then a surjective etale scheme chart $w:W\to A_T\times_{B_T}V$, as supplied by [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The scheme map $q:W\to V$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation: its space projection is a base change of $h_T$, and $w$ is etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation; use base-change and composition stability [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] and the agreement of chart properties with scheme properties [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. The projection $A_T\times_{B_T}V\to A_T$ is etale as a base change of $v$. Thus $r:W\to A_T$ is etale. Etale implies smooth, locally of finite presentation and locally of finite type, so $pr:W\to T$ is locally of finite type by the calculus node. It equals the composite $W\xrightarrow{q}V\to T$ because both maps are the projection to $T$.

source.place: Tag 06EW (lemma-locally-finite-type-fppf-local-source), through the etale presentation construction in Tag 06ER (lemma-transfer-from-schemes)

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent] to the scheme maps $W\xrightarrow{q}V\to T$: the preceding step verifies exactly its surjectivity, flatness, local-finite-presentation and composite-local-finite-type hypotheses. It gives that $V\to T$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to $B_T\to T$, with target chart $T\to T$ the identity and source chart $V\to B_T$. It follows that $B_T\to T$ is locally of finite type. Since $T\to\mathcal C$ was arbitrary, this is precisely the scheme-base-change test for $g$ in the item. Neither charts nor $q$ were assumed quasi-compact, and no Noetherian hypothesis was used.
